title: ARD container (FF12AR03, 10 sections)

container.notes: Little-endian. 0x30-byte header: 8-byte magic 'FF12AR03', then 10 u32 section offsets relative to the ARD start (0 = absent). Also found as section 19 of an EBP. Physical order: sections 0,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9 each zero-padded to 16, then section 1 last with no padding after it. Section length = next larger non-zero offset minus this offset (end of ARD for the highest). Sections 2, 4, 7, 8 are st2e tables (84, 88, 56, 56-byte entries).

records.name: ardHeader
records.where: ARD offset 0 (standalone file offset 0, or start of EBP section 19)

fields.name: sectionOffset00
fields.notes: Section 0: unknown. 0 = absent. Section names: enum ArdSection.

fields.name: sectionOffset01
fields.notes: Section 1: models (u32 count + 8-byte entries). Must be the physically last section, no padding after it.

fields.name: sectionOffset07
fields.notes: Section 7: default stats, st2e with 56-byte entries.

fields.name: sectionOffset08
fields.notes: Section 8: additive stats, st2e with 56-byte entries.

fields.name: sectionOffset09
fields.notes: Section 9: special action animations (u32 count, entries from +0x10, 16 bytes each).

records.name: ardModelEntry
records.where: ARD section 1, starting at section offset +4 (after a u32 entry count at +0)

roundTrip: Write sections 0,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9 in that order, each at a 16-byte boundary followed by zero padding; then write section 1 last with no trailing padding.
When the ARD lives in EBP section 19, rebuild the ARD first, then recompute the EBP offsets that follow section 19.
gaps: Reason section 1 must be last is not documented.
Meaning of the u32 flags in section 1 entries.
Not verified whether vanilla standalone ARD files end unpadded after section 1.
